last_transition_reason: The proof correctly rewrites the q-Pochhammer quotient as the finite interval product, expands each factor via the cyclotomic factorization of q^N-1, identifies the exponent of each Phi_d with M_d(r+a,r+b)-M_d(a,b), and then proves the consequence from polynomiality by a standard primitive-root contradiction argument. The argument matches the lemma statement and its role in the assembly, and it does not rely on any forbidden ancestry result.
latest_nl_proof:
Let e_d := M_d(r+a,r+b) - M_d(a,b) for each positive integer d. First rewrite the quotient of q-Pochhammer symbols. Since a <= b and r >= 0, we have (q;q)_{r+b}/(q;q)_{r+a} = product_{t=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1 - q^t) and (q;q)_a/(q;q)_b = 1 / product_{t=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^t). Therefore
R_{a,b,r}(q) = product_{i=a+1}^{b} (1 - q^{r+i})/(1 - q^i),
with the empty product equal to 1 when a=b.

Now use the defining factorization of cyclotomic polynomials: for every positive integer N,
q^N - 1 = product_{d | N} Phi_d(q).
For each i with a+1 <= i <= b,
(1 - q^{r+i})/(1 - q^i) = (q^{r+i} - 1)/(q^i - 1) = (product_{d | (r+i)} Phi_d(q)) / (product_{d | i} Phi_d(q)).
Multiplying over i from a+1 to b and collecting equal cyclotomic factors, we get an identity of rational functions
R_{a,b,r}(q) = product_{d >= 1} Phi_d(q)^(A_d - B_d),
where
A_d := |{ i in Z : a < i <= b and d divides (r+i) }|,
B_d := |{ i in Z : a < i <= b and d divides i }|.
If d > r+b, then necessarily d > b as well, so both A_d and B_d are 0. Hence only finitely many exponents are nonzero, so this product is well defined.

It remains to identify A_d and B_d with the M_d counts. The map i -> m := r+i is a bijection from the set counted by A_d onto the set { m in Z : r+a < m <= r+b and d divides m }. Therefore A_d = M_d(r+a,r+b). Also, by definition, B_d = M_d(a,b). Substituting these equalities gives
R_{a,b,r}(q) = product_{d >= 1} Phi_d(q)^( M_d(r+a,r+b) - M_d(a,b) ),
which is the claimed cyclotomic factorization.

For the consequence, assume that R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q]. Let I_+ := { d >= 1 : e_d > 0 } and I_- := { d >= 1 : e_d < 0 }. These sets are finite because e_d = 0 for d > r+b. The factorization above can then be written as
R_{a,b,r}(q) = (product_{d in I_+} Phi_d(q)^{e_d}) / (product_{d in I_-} Phi_d(q)^{-e_d}).
Suppose, for contradiction, that I_- is nonempty. Choose D in I_-. Since R_{a,b,r}(q) is actually a polynomial, say P(q) in Z[q], clearing denominators yields the polynomial identity over C,
P(q) product_{d in I_-} Phi_d(q)^{-e_d} = product_{d in I_+} Phi_d(q)^{e_d}.
Now let zeta be a primitive D-th root of unity. By the defining root property of cyclotomic polynomials, Phi_D(zeta)=0, and for every d != D one has Phi_d(zeta) != 0 because zeta is not a primitive d-th root of unity. Evaluating the cleared polynomial identity at q=zeta, the left-hand side is 0 because it contains the factor Phi_D(zeta)^{-e_D} with -e_D > 0, while the right-hand side is nonzero because none of its factors vanish at zeta. This contradiction shows that I_- must be empty.

Thus e_d >= 0 for every positive integer d, i.e.
M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b)
for every positive integer d. This is exactly the stated consequence.

statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define (q;q)_0 := 1 and (q;q)_n := product_{t=1}^n (1 - q^t) for n >= 1, and define R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b). For each positive integer d, define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|. Then one has the cyclotomic factorization R_{a,b,r}(q) = product_{d>=1} Phi_d(q)^( M_d(r+a,r+b) - M_d(a,b) ), where Phi_d(q) is the d-th cyclotomic polynomial. Consequently, if R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q], then M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d.

domain_restrictions: a and b are integers with a less than or equal to b and both are nonnegative.
q is treated as a formal variable, not as a specified numeric value.
n is a nonnegative integer in the q-Pochhammer definition.
t ranges over positive integers from 1 to n in the finite product.
u and v are integer endpoints when evaluating M_d.
m is an integer counted in the definition of M_d.
The cyclotomic product over all positive integers d has only finitely many nontrivial factors because the exponents vanish for large d.
The implication about Z[q] concerns integer-coefficient polynomials, not merely rational functions.
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every choice of integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, the rational q-expression R_{a,b,r}(q) factors into cyclotomic polynomials with exponent at index d equal to the difference between the number of multiples of d in the interval from r+a to r+b and the number of multiples of d in the interval from a to b. If this expression is actually a polynomial with integer coefficients, then every such exponent is nonnegative, so the count of multiples of d in the shifted interval is at least the count in the original interval for every positive integer d.
quantifier_order: For all integers a and b with 0 <= a <= b, and all integers r with r >= 0.
For each nonnegative integer n, define the q-Pochhammer symbol using a product over t from 1 to n.
For each positive integer d, define M_d(u,v) as the number of integers m satisfying u < m <= v and d divides m.
For all such a, b, and r, the stated cyclotomic factorization of R_{a,b,r}(q) holds as an identity in the formal variable q.
For all such a, b, and r, if R_{a,b,r}(q) lies in Z[q], then for every positive integer d one has M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b).
